Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the run chase! The umpires are out in the middle and so are the players of Pakistan Under-19. It will be the pairing of Harry Dixon and Sam Konstas to open the innings for Australia Under-19. Ubaid Shah, the fiery right-arm pacer will get things underway with the ball. Let's play...
... The Run Chase ...

Australia Under-19 did well with the ball and Hugh Weibgen's decision to bowl first might just work out for them in these conditions. Their pacers paved the way for the others to build pressure. Callum Vidler and Mahli Beardman troubled the batters early on in the powerplay but it was Tom Straker who gave them their first breakthrough, soon followed by Callum Vidler. Tom Straker wasn’t done yet as he got rid of the opposition skipper as well. Rafael Macmillan, the spinner trapped Ahmad Hassan in front of the stumps. Tom Straker came in and cleaned Haroon Arshad up soon after. After that for 10 overs, the batters found their rhythm and scored some runs but Straker was brought back in and he got rid of the dangerous Azan Awais. Tom Campbell, sent Arafat Minhas, the other batter in form back to the dugout and after that, it was a quick few overs to wind up the innings. Ubaid Shah, Mohammad Zeeshan, and Ali Raza all were dismissed by Tom Straker as he reached his six-wicket haul. It is a memorable day for him and he will hope that his teammates with the bat will make it even special with a victory. They have to get to the 180-run mark in 50 overs which is very easy but they will have to be careful of the pace attack of the opposition as well as Pakistan Under-19 did bolw out Bangaldesh for 150 while defending just 155 runs, so, there's a lot to play for. Stay tuned and we will be back for the chase in a short while.

Tom Straker, the man of the moment for Australia Under-19 is down for a quick chat. He says that they did talk about bowling it on a consistent length before the game and adds that he loves bowling to the right-handers more but got lucky against the lefties. Adds that he wanted to bowl more short balls as there was some bounce in the deck and it came off.

SIXFER FOR Tom Straker and courtesy of his spell, Pakistan Under-19 have been bowled out for 179. Pakistan Under-19 had a bat outing with the bat in hand. They started off poorly and went into defensive mode. They failed to express themselves in the Powerplay and lost their openers, Shamyl Hussain and Shahzaib Khan towards the end of it. Saad Baig, their skipper also couldn’t step up to the occasion and crumbled under pressure. Ahmad Hassan was trapped in front of the stumps, trying to play a poor shot. Haroon Arshad too, departed after a long struggle out in the middle. Azan Awais, who came in at number 3 batted with confidence and completed his half-century but couldn’t take the innings deep. Arafat Minhas also reached his fifty and got out the very next ball trying to play a poor shot. Ubaid Shah played one good shot but then got out on the very next ball as he wanted to be over-aggressive. Mohammad Zeeshan and Ali Raza, were cleaned up in two consecutive deliveries to wind up the innings. Arafat Minhas and Azan Awais together made up 104 runs and none of the others could cross 20 runs individually. They end up with 179 on the board which is a low score at this stage and this leaves their bowlers with a lot of work to do in the second innings.

OUT! KNOCKED HIM OVER! Tom Straker ends with a six-fer, the best bowling effort in a semi-final or final of the Under-19 World Cup ever (6 for 24 runs). Bowls it quick and a bit full on middle, angling it in. Ali Raza stays leg side and backs away a bit to play it square on the off side but is beaten for raw pacer. The ball smahses into the leg stump again and yet again, the stump is uprooted as Pakistan Under-19 are bundled out for 179 runs.

The umpires are out in the middle and the players of Australia Under-19 also take to the field after huddling up around the boundary ropes. We are just a few minutes away from the start of the game. But first, the two sets of players along with their mascots will line up for their respective national anthems. It will be the national anthem of Pakistan first followed by the Australian national anthem.

PITCH REPORT - Samuel Badree is pitchside. He says that there is a breeze coming in from the north-eastern side. Adds that on either side it is a similar boundary but down the ground, it is a long hit at 84 meters. Marina Iqbal joins him and says that there is a fair bit of live grass on it but it is dry as well and the pacers will get purchase early on. Reckons that it will get a bit slower as the game goes on.

Saad Baig, the captain of Pakistan Under-19 says that they wanted to bat first anyway. Adds that the conditions look good but the batters need to take a bit of time early on and in the first 10 overs, they need to be a bit careful. Informs that they have one change in the team.

Australia Under-19 skipper, Hugh Weibgen says that they will bowl first because the pitch conditions allow them to exploit it in the first innings and hopes that it gets better for batting over time. Says that they are looking forward to playing their first match here. Mentions his team's balance and reckons that they have been playing spin well and ends by informing that there are three changes to the Playing XI.

The highly-rated Ubaid Shah then stepped up and made the big occasion his own with a five-wicket haul that even won the game for his side. The match is all set to be a fine clash with some exciting batting talent and pace bowlers in both camps raring to take on each other. Which side will come out on top though? Following a riveting 1st semi-final between India and South Africa, where the defending champions secured their fifth successive final berth, attention now turns to the 2nd semi-final of the 2024 Under-19 World Cup between Australia Under-19 and Pakistan Under-19 at Willowmoore Park in Benoni. Both teams are unbeaten heading into the semi-final as they vie for a spot in the final of the 2024 Under-19 World Cup. For the three-time champions, Australia, it has been their top order of Sam Konstas, Harry Dixon, and skipper Hugh Weibgen that have done the bulk of the scoring. Harjas Singh, Tom Campbell, and Ryan Hicks do not have runs under their belt, and they will be tested in this crunch game. On the bowling front, right-arm pacer Callum Vidler has led the charge and helped the Aussies set the tone upfront. Tom Straker and Mahli Beardman have offered good support to Vidler to keep the pressure on the opposition. In the spin department, it has been Rafael Macmillan who has stood out. Like Australia, Pakistan too have had a spotless run in the tournament. Left-handed opener Shahzaib Khan has done the heavy lifting for the Asian side, while his opening partner, Shamyl Hussain, has shown glimpses of promise, as has Ahmad Hassan. Skipper Saad Baig and Azan Awais are yet to come to the party, and there can be no better time than a World Cup semi-final.
